rootCause.details: Both solutions identify the Unicode-regexp grammar issue: backslash-hyphen is an invalid identity escape outside a character class under the u flag, so hyphen must be removed from the ordinary backslash-escaped operator class and encoded separately.

behavior.details: The accepted fix emits `\u002d`; the solver emits `\x2d`. Both are fixed-width escapes for the same U+002D code point, compile in Unicode and non-Unicode JavaScript patterns, work inside character classes, and match literal hyphens without consuming adjacent hexadecimal-looking characters.

tests.details: Both add focused Unicode compilation and literal-match coverage. The solver additionally asserts its exact escaped phrase and preserves the non-string TypeError contract. Independent probes covered repeated and adjacent hyphens, Unicode text, every existing metacharacter, both regexp modes, grouping, and character-class placement.

scope.details: Both patches change only index.js and test.js, leave all other operator escaping intact, and add no runtime dependency or API surface.

simplicity.details: The accepted patch inlines both regular expressions and documents the Unicode grammar; the solver names the operator and hyphen expressions separately. Both implementations are clear and comparably small.

regressions.details: No semantic divergence was found between `\x2d` and `\u002d` across direct probes. The frozen solver also passed the package suite, lint, declarations, syntax, packaging, and independent round-trip cases.

limitations: The emitted escaped string differs textually from the accepted fix (`\x2d` versus `\u002d`), so consumers asserting a specific serialization would observe a difference; no exact serialization was part of the issue acceptance.
The historical package suite required Node 12 and a transient @types/node@12 pin, while direct behavior probes ran on Node 24.
Only JavaScript RegExp semantics were audited; cross-engine regular-expression dialect compatibility was not part of the frozen acceptance.
